Subject: POC ownership roster & trial ops — next steps

Hi Alice / Bob,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. I wanted to capture the follow-ups and propose a tight ops plan so we can kick the POC next week. Key items below — please confirm owners and any conflicting timelines from your side.

1) Success criteria (proposed)
   - Inference latency: median < 200ms p95 < 400ms for representative traffic (see attached sample load)
   - Cost proxy: tokens / second baseline and target (sheet attached)
   - Functional: correctness on 10 canned queries and 3 integration flows (detailed in Drive doc)

2) Minimum test plan / timeline
   - Kickoff call (1hr): Mon 8 Mar, 10:00 PT (tentative)
   - Provision infra & access: 1–2 business days
   - Run smoke tests + baseline: days 2–3
   - Full evaluation window: days 4–10 (1 week)

3) Ownership / RACI (please reply with names) — initial draft
   - Redwood (solution): Benchmarks, model serving, trial configuration 
   - Acme (app owner): Integration, sample payloads, success criteria sign-off 
   - Acme (infra): VPC, network rules, egress policy 
   - Procurement: PO / contract sign-off

Attachments: poc-success-metrics.xlsx (baseline templates), infra-ownership-diagram.png

Next steps / asks for Acme:
   - Confirm infra owner (who will do the VPC/network setup)
   - Confirm app owner and test payload owner
   - Approve kickoff slot or propose alternatives

I’m copying Karthik (solutions) and Monica (CS) to loop infra and success playbooks. Happy to split this into a brief mutual action plan after you confirm owners.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
phone: (415) 555-0192

Thanks Tessa — this is helpful. Quick answers from my side:

- Infra owner: Bob Chen (cc'd) will own the VPC and network setup. He has lead time to provision on Mon/Tue.
- App owner: I'm the product owner for the integration; I will nominate our lead engineer (Diego Ramos) to work with your team on payloads.
- Procurement: looping procurement to start POC SOW review. They should be able to sign a short MSA + SOW within ~5 business days.

Two notes:
- Can Redwood provide a small template for the network policy (egress IPs / ports) — that will speed our infra work.
- For success criteria, can we add one business KPI: average error rate < 1% on the 3 integration flows?

I can confirm the kickoff 8 Mar 10:00 PT if Bob confirms provisioning.

Best,

Hi all — Ben from Solutions (infra & deployment). Quick follow-up on the two asks: network template and the RACI.

1) Network template: attaching a one-page checklist below (I also dropped a diagram in Drive). Minimum egress we need: outbound to s3 (443), Redwood control plane (443) and model-serving endpoints (443). Static egress IPs are not strictly required for the trial — we can also accept a short-lived NAT rule; see the doc for both options.

2) Proposed RACI table (high level):
   - Provision VPC & FW rules: Responsible = Bob Chen (Acme), Accountable = Ben Carter (Redwood), Consulted = Karthik Iyer, Informed = Tessa Morgan
   - Payload integration: Responsible = Diego Ramos (Acme), Accountable = Alice Ramos (Acme), Consulted = Monica Patel, Informed = Karthik Iyer
   - Success criteria sign-off: Responsible = Alice Ramos, Accountable = Acme Product Lead, Consulted = Monica Patel, Informed = Tessa Morgan
   - Procurement / SOW: Responsible = Procurement (Acme), Accountable = Alice Ramos, Consulted = Tessa Morgan, Informed = Ben Carter

3) Timeline tweak: If Acme can provision on Mon/Tue we'll keep kickoff 8 Mar. If provisioning slips, propose Wed 10 Mar as backup.

Attachments referenced: poc-success-metrics.xlsx (template), infra-ownership-diagram.png (ownership callouts).
